nodes.label: Research question: detect friction without load/speed false alarms

nodes.norm_label: research question: detect friction without load/speed false alarms
nodes.rationale: Torque and tracking error also rise for heavier loads and faster motion, so a naive detector would false-alarm; problem split into detect, diagnose, estimate wear (wear needs run-to-failure data, out of scope).

nodes.label: Payload vs friction fault separability
nodes.rationale: Heavier payload (2.0 kg vs 0.5 kg) mainly shifts joint torque RMS higher (J1 ~30-60 to ~40-83 N m) while tracking error stays similar (J1 ~0-6 mrad, J2 ~2-19 mrad). Friction x3 raises tracking error along motion (J1 ~5-11 mrad, J2 ~20-34 mrad) across the whole torque range. Torque alone cannot separate load from friction; tracking error separates them, most cleanly on joint 2 where clusters do not overlap.

nodes.label: Stage A: Physics simulation
nodes.rationale: No real robot, so friction effects must arise through physics equations rather than faked signals; armature added to M for discrete-time PD stability at 100 Hz; controller must not read faulty friction or the fault becomes invisible / leaks the answer.

nodes.label: PD controller with gravity compensation (100 Hz, ZOH)
nodes.norm_label: pd controller with gravity compensation (100 hz, zoh)
nodes.rationale: Does not know or compensate friction, so increased friction shows up as larger error and PD torque.

nodes.label: Friction model b*q' + tau_c*tanh(q'/eps)
nodes.rationale: tanh smooths Coulomb discontinuity; sign() would make numerical integration chatter.

nodes.label: 2-DOF planar arm dynamics M(q)q'' + C q' + G + tau_f = tau
nodes.norm_label: 2-dof planar arm dynamics m(q)q'' + c q' + g + tau_f = tau
nodes.rationale: Accelerations by Gaussian elimination, not matrix inversion; payload merged into link 2 so it affects both M and G.
